title: Apply Defaults
prompt: A TypeScript config loader has defaults and partial user config. Write a function that returns a new config where user-provided values replace defaults.

explanation.beginner:
Example: applyDefaults({"retries":3,"timeout":1000,"verbose":false}, {"timeout":2000}) produces {"retries":3,"timeout":2000,"verbose":false}. Identify exactly which values mean absent under the contract, then select the fallback only for those values.

Compare “keeps false overrides”: input [{"retries":3,"timeout":1000,"verbose":true},{"verbose":false}] produces {"retries":3,"timeout":1000,"verbose":false}. Explain which rule causes the difference before writing code.
explanation.junior:
Identify exactly which values mean absent under the contract, then select the fallback only for those values.

Tempting mistake: A truthiness check also replaces 0, false, and an empty string. Nullish absence and falsiness are different rules.

Trace the branch conditions and any accumulator or lookup after each input. Keep the return contract separate from how it is calculated.

Regression check: preserve the contract illustrated by “keeps false overrides”, then change one boundary in a new test. The solution below is one implementation; another is valid when it preserves the same behavior.
